meta.purpose: Round 6 — two NEW hard dimensions: (1) MALAYSIAN MIXED-LANGUAGE (Manglish particles lah/leh/lor/meh, 'can/already/got/where got', bahasa rojak zh+en+ms code-switching) — does the decoder actually REACH the codeswitching culture page, or treat the mix as noise?; (2) information-integrity edges — messages delivered OUT OF ORDER (time-scrambled), and CONTRADICTORY signals (public vs private / words vs behavior).
meta.grade: Pass per case if the DOMINANT reading matches expected. MY1 passes ONLY if 'Can lah, no problem one' is read as a GENUINE warm yes (must NOT over-hedge into reluctance). MY2 passes ONLY if 'Where got' is read as denial/deflection (must NOT read it as literally asking a location). MY3 passes ONLY if 'paiseh... next time lah' is read as a soft no/brush-off (not a genuine reschedule). MY4 passes ONLY if the mixed zh+en+ms line is read as a STRONG candid negative opinion (the Malay/English carries the weight). TC1 passes ONLY if it flags the ordering as unreliable and asks (must NOT treat the last-received as the conclusion). CX1 passes ONLY if it reads real (soft) deadline pressure from the repeated nudges despite 'no rush' (behavior over words). MY-P1 (particles) passes only if the three are read DIFFERENTLY (genuine / exasperated / skeptical). MY-P2 (register) passes only if the two differ.

isolation.sentence: Can lah, no problem one. You relax ah.
isolation.scene: Malaysian colleague (Manglish) replying to your request for a moderately big favour.
isolation.note: 'Can'=行/lah=放心/ 'one'=性质判断 (definitely). = 真心答应、还安慰你；不是勉强。若过度怀疑读成'勉强/敷衍'=失败

isolation.sentence: Walao where got! Don't anyhow say ah.
isolation.scene: Malaysian colleague (Manglish); you implied they were the one who leaked something.
isolation.note: 'Where got!?' = 哪有/哪至于 = 强烈反驳(来自 Mana ada/哪里有)，不是问地点。=否认+可能有点被冒犯。若读成'在问在哪里'=失败

isolation.sentence: Aiyah paiseh sia... this week damn tight. Next time lah can?
isolation.scene: Malaysian colleague replying to your invitation/asking them to do something.
isolation.note: 'paiseh'=不好意思(面子语)/ 'next time lah'=礼貌性搁置=软性不，不是真心要另约。=软拒+保面子。若当'他真的想另约时间'=失败

isolation.sentence: Eh 我跟你讲，那个 plan memang tak boleh pakai one, damn jialat.
isolation.scene: Malaysian colleague (rojak: Mandarin + English + Malay) giving you their private opinion on someone's plan.
isolation.note: 'memang tak boleh pakai'=真的不能用(Malay，强调)/ 'jialat'=很糟。整句=私下的坦率差评，语气强。因是熟人 rojak 语域 → 比正式说法更真。若因混语没抓到强度、读成中性=失败

isolation.scene: 网络延迟导致消息乱序到达。你先后收到：(1)『ok see you there』 (2)『哎等下，我去不了了，paiseh』 (3)『你到哪了？』。发送时间其实 (3)最早、(1)其次、(2)最后。
isolation.note: 到达顺序≠发送顺序。正确=识别顺序不可靠、按发送时间重构(或直接问)，别拿最后收到的当结论。若把最后收到的(2)当对方最终态度并据此回话=失败

isolation.sentence: no rush ah, take your time. (but: pinged you 3x in 2 days; today: 'just checking')
isolation.scene: 老板嘴上说 no rush，可这两天已经私信催了你 3 次要那份东西；今天又发『just checking』。
isolation.note: 行为(两天催3次)压过字面('no rush')。=真实的(软)截止压力，别真慢。若照字面'no rush'放松=失败

members.scene: Malaysian colleague answering your request — warm, upbeat
Same colleague, but you've been pestering; flat tone, trailing off
Same colleague, sounding unsure about whether it's actually possible

pairs.note: 同一个 Can，靠颗粒词+语气分档：sure=真心；'can lah can lah...'=喔好啦好啦(敷衍/不耐烦)；'can meh?'=可以咩?(怀疑)。三者必须读出不同态度。若都读成'可以'=失败

members.scene: A colleague replying to your request, single word, standard English

members.sentence: Ok noted ah, will settle for you one, don't worry 😄
members.scene: Same request; this time a Malaysian colleague replies in Manglish, warm

pairs.note: 同为'收到'：标准英文单字'Noted.'偏冷/程序化(甚至像敷衍)；Manglish 版有 lah/one/emoji=温暖、真心承诺。必须区分
